deck.rule: potency bins with fixed quotas, Butina clusters at Tanimoto 0.6 inside each bin taken largest cluster first with up to 4 analogues per cluster, approved drugs pinned on top of the quotas
deck.source: ChEMBL_37 (released 2026-05-01), target CHEMBL203 EGFR, IC50 nM, relation '=', assay_type B, pchembl present, no data_validity_comment, wild type assays only
deck.map: t-SNE on Tanimoto distance (1024 bit Morgan r2), perplexity 20, random_state 42, init random, scaled uniformly into 1000 x 700 with 30 unit margin
deck.disclosure: This deck is reweighted toward weak compounds. ChEMBL over-represents potent EGFR inhibitors, so the potency mix here does not match the published record.

game.uncertainty: 1 minus the highest Tanimoto to anything measured

model.kind: similarity weighted k nearest neighbours, 1024 bit Morgan r2
model.v1_note: on the first deck, picked for maximum diversity, the same model scored -0.14 hits against random and the gate failed

dock.box: 27.1 x 16.4 x 17.9 Angstrom, centred on the crystal ligand
dock.prep: dimorphite_dl 2.0.2 top protomer at pH 7.4, RDKit AddHs, ETKDGv3 seed 42, MMFF94, Meeko mk_prepare_ligand

md.verdict_rule: a pose holds if the median ligand heavy atom RMSD over the last 1 ns is under 2.5 A in at least 2 of 3 seeds, written before any trajectory was run

provenance: Protein: PDB 1M17, the EGFR kinase domain with erlotinib bound. Waters out, missing atoms rebuilt, hydrogens added at pH 7.4.
Docking: AutoDock Vina, one box, fixed seed. Redocking the crystal pose returns it to 1.41 Angstrom, so the setup can reproduce a known answer.
Compounds: ChEMBL_37, target CHEMBL203. 302 of 8,146 curated ones, picked as analogue clusters inside five potency bins. 36 reach pIC50 8.

Model: k nearest neighbours on Morgan fingerprints, running in this browser. Leave one out error 0.79 log units. Over 200 simulated games it found 1.19 more strong compounds than random picking, against a bar of 0.7 set before the run.

On a deck picked for diversity instead of analogues the same model did no better than chance, because it needs near neighbours to learn from. That is why this deck is built from analogue series, as a screening library is.
Docking and molecular dynamics are physics. The screening model is the machine learning part.
Molecular dynamics: OpenMM, ff14SB protein, TIP3P water, 0.15 M salt, 2 ns per run, 3 seeds per pose. A few nanoseconds can show a pose falling apart. It cannot measure how tightly a drug binds.
The picture is a flat projection of a real structure. Depth is shading.
Every number was computed before you arrived. Nothing here calls a server or a language model. Versions, seeds and box sizes are in data/fitdrug/meta.json.
